issues.detail: The Greek 'πειθομεν' (peithomen) is a present passive/middle verb meaning 'we are persuaded' or 'we are being persuaded.' The Vietnamese 'thuyết phục' means 'to persuade' (active), reversing the direction of the action.

The Greek 'θεω' (theō) is a noun meaning 'God.' The Vietnamese 'Đức Chúa Trời đã tỏ ra chúng tôi' translates to 'God has revealed us/shown us,' whereas the Greek 'θεω δε πεφανερωμεθα' means 'but we are being revealed to God' (passive voice).
